sections.h2: Where is Spokane and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Spokane sits on the Spokane River in eastern Washington, about 18 miles from the Idaho line, and it is the seat of Spokane County. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 230,783 residents, which makes it the second-largest city in the state after Seattle. The city was incorporated on November 29, 1881 and covers about 69 square miles at an elevation near 1,844 feet.

The street grid runs on the compass. Division Street splits the city into east and west, Sprague Avenue splits it into north and south, and Interstate 90 crosses the middle. Downtown is the Riverside neighborhood, and the South Hill rises to the south. Browne's Addition, west of downtown, was the city's first prestigious address and holds Queen Anne and Craftsman mansions. Hillyard, in the northeast, grew around the Great Northern rail yard. West Central, East Central and the University District, where Gonzaga and the WSU Spokane health sciences campus sit, fill in the rest of the core.

Spokane Public Schools, organized in 1889, is the largest district in the city. The Mead district serves north Spokane County outside the city limits. Which district a house falls into changes its school levy, so check the address on the county's parcel record.

sections.h2: What do Spokane's housing numbers look like?
sections.html:
Spokane houses are older and less expensive than most of the Puget Sound market, and rentals make up a large share of homes. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures set the city beside the county:

Climate is part of owning here. Spokane has cold winters and a dry summer pattern, with about 16.5 inches of precipitation a year, and more frequent wildfire smoke in summer since the late 20th century. The warmest month is July at about 71 degrees on average and the coolest is December at about 29 degrees.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax for a Spokane house?
sections.html:
The city does not send the bill. The Spokane County Treasurer bills and collects the tax, and the Spokane County Assessor sets the value. The City of Spokane is one of the roughly 56 taxing districts in the county that send budgets to the Assessor each November.

City property tax goes mainly into the General Fund, which pays for police, fire, streets, parks and the library. The city's 2025 to 2026 budget overview assumed it would levy the 1% increase allowed on regular levies, and it lists a streets levy and a public safety personnel levy fund among its dedicated revenue. Other lines on a Spokane bill come from the county, the school district, the state school levy and any special districts that cover the parcel.

Water, sewer, solid waste and other enterprise services are supported entirely by fees, not property tax. If you are selling, ask the city's utility billing office whether any utility balance is outstanding on the address.

  • Treasurer: Spokane County Courthouse, 1116 W. Broadway Ave., 509-477-4713, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
  • Assessor: 509-477-3698.
  • Mail payments to the Spokane County Treasurer, P.O. Box 199, Spokane, WA 99210.

sections.h2: When is Spokane property tax due?
sections.html:
Spokane property tax is due in two halves, April 30 and October 31, and a bill under $50 is due in full on April 30. If a date lands on a weekend or county holiday, the Treasurer accepts payment the next business day. The second half for 2026 was due October 31, 2026, so the next date on the calendar is April 30, 2027.

The statement arrives once a year with two coupons. If yours has not shown up by March 31, call 509-477-4713 or find it online on SCOUT. Mortgage companies may pay the tax from escrow, but the county says it does not bill them directly or keep their information, so confirm with your lender.

The courthouse has two drop boxes that accept checks only. In the two weeks before each due date, the Treasurer has also collected in person at Spokane Valley City Hall and the North Spokane Library. Mail is sorted by federal postmark, and the Treasurer warns that postal changes have delayed postmarks, so mail early. The office is closed Thursday and Friday, November 26 and 27, 2026.

sections.h2: What does late Spokane property tax cost?
sections.html:
Late tax in Spokane is charged interest beginning May 1 for the first half and November 1 for the second half, calculated on the full year's amount. A home with four or fewer units pays 0.75% per month and no penalty, while other property pays 1% per month plus a 3% penalty on June 1 and 8% on December 1.

State law gives the Treasurer discretion for payment agreements and partial payments on current and past-due taxes, with money applied to the oldest year first (RCW 84.56.020). A hardship waiver for a death of a spouse, parent or stepparent requires notice within 60 days of the due date (RCW 84.56.025). Spokane County says it cannot waive interest when the statement went to an address given by the taxpayer or the taxpayer's agent, such as a closing agent.

A payment that the bank returns carries a $30 fee, plus the interest, penalty and costs that apply.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Spokane assessment?
sections.html:
Property in the city of Spokane is appealed through the Spokane County Board of Equalization, not through City Hall. File the petition form by July 1 of the assessment year or within 30 days after the Change of Value Notice was mailed, whichever is later. There is no fee, and a call or letter will not count in place of the form.

The board looks only at market value. It will not consider the amount of tax, the percentage increase, other properties' values or personal hardship. Bring comparable sales close to January 1 of the assessment year, since the assessor is presumed correct and your evidence must be clear, cogent and convincing (RCW 84.40.0301). Additional evidence is due seven business days before the hearing, and the board mails notice of a hearing 15 business days ahead.

Talk to the Assessor first at 509-477-3698. Many disagreements end with a stipulation of value. If you lose, you have 30 calendar days to go to the State Board of Tax Appeals. The county Assessor revalues all parcels each year and inspects each one at least once every six years.

sections.h2: What relief exists for Spokane homeowners?
sections.html:
Seniors, people retired because of disability and certain veterans can apply for a property tax exemption through the Spokane County Assessor at 509-477-3698. The Treasurer's page says that Senate Bill 6162, signed after the 2026 session, will change the income thresholds starting in 2027, so ask about the limits that apply to you rather than relying on older numbers.

Every tax statement must carry a notice about the exemption and the state deferral program (RCW 84.56.020). Owners who are income-qualified, live in the home and face a tax foreclosure action can have interest and penalties waived about three years after delinquency, once, per property.

If you recently bought and paid under 90% of the assessed value after July 1 and before December 31 of the assessment year, the Board of Equalization may reconvene after the usual deadline. Ask the board's office about timing.

sections.h2: What should you do about back taxes when selling in Spokane?
sections.html:
Ask the Treasurer for a payoff covering every year owed, give it to the closing agent, and confirm the agent has your correct parcel number and mailing address. Spokane County will not waive interest if its statement was mailed to the address a closing agent supplied.

The state's real estate excise tax is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale. The Department of Revenue lists graduated state rates for sales starting January 1, 2027 of 1.1% up to $551,000, 1.28% on the portion from $551,000 to $1,551,000, 2.75% to $3,051,000 and 3.0% above, with a local rate added on top. Usually the seller pays.

Waiting can be risky. When tax stays unpaid three years after delinquency, the treasurer must start foreclosure by certificate of delinquency (RCW 84.64.050). Spokane homes with deferred maintenance or an inherited title often face this deadline, so do the payoff math early.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Spokane?
faqs.a: The Spokane County Treasurer, at 1116 W. Broadway Ave. or P.O. Box 199, Spokane, WA 99210, or online. Call 509-477-4713. The city itself does not collect the tax.

faqs.q: When is Spokane property tax due?
faqs.a: April 30 and October 31, with bills under $50 due in full April 30. The October 31, 2026 date has passed, so the next one is April 30, 2027, or the following business day if that falls on a weekend.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Spokane property value?
faqs.a: File a petition with the Spokane County Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year or within 30 days of the Change of Value Notice, whichever is later. It is free, and you must show market value evidence, such as comparable sales.

faqs.q: What interest applies to late Spokane property tax?
faqs.a: For a home with four or fewer units, 0.75% a month with no penalty. For other property, 1% a month plus 3% on June 1 and 8% on December 1. The charge applies to the whole year's tax.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Spokane house that owes back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax, interest and penalties are paid from the proceeds at closing. Call the Spokane County Treasurer for a payoff, and give the closing agent your correct parcel number and mailing address.
